heroHeadline: CDMX Congress Passes Electoral and Anti-Extortion Reforms as Metro Line 3 Derails and Tepito Turf War Escalates
heroSubtitle: Mexico City's Congress had a busy mid-August: on August 14 it approved a federal electoral reform capping regidor seats and legislature budgets (49-16), and on August 15 it unanimously passed anti-extortion reforms creating a new 'coercive harassment' offense with 10-to-15-year sentences. On infrastructure, an unoccupied Metro Line 3 car derailed August 14 at the Ticomán workshop — officials blamed rain-softened, geologically unstable ground — while heavy storms on August 11 flooded the Reforma/Chapultepec corridor and felled trees across 13 of 16 alcaldías. On security, a Unión Tepito vs. Anti-Unión turf war in the Centro Histórico has left 24 dead in 2026, including a 17-year-old killed August 10 in Tepito, even as SSC touted a 16.4% year-over-year citywide homicide decline and detained 55 alleged faction members; escorts also foiled an attempted robbery of C5 coordinator Salvador Guerrero Chiprés on August 11. Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada marked International Youth Day (Aug 12) by pledging to expand university scholarships to 200,000 students and pilot 1,000 affordable rental units, and thousands marched from the Ángel de la Independencia to the Zócalo on August 9 for the International Day of Indigenous Peoples.
